params.body:
Two things, and the second is why the first was invisible.

**Werking belongs with Inzichten.** Both are about the platform itself and about nobody's
vehicles; Beheer is the settings of somebody's garage, which is a different question. Clicking
Inzichten still opens the figures, exactly as it did when that was the only screen there, and
Werking hangs under it. The parent stays a link the same way Biedingen does.

**And it was invisible anyway, which is the real find.** The rights of a user are written into the
session when he signs in, and nothing ever revisits them. So a menu added today reaches somebody
only when he signs out and signs in again — which is why a brand new screen was invisible to the
administrator who had just added it.

The session now carries which generation of the rights tables it came from: the youngest change to
a menu or to a role's access, asked at most once a minute for the whole platform. When that no
longer matches, the rights are rebuilt. A session from before this carries no generation and is
left alone — it keeps working exactly as it did and heals itself at the next sign-in — so nobody
is logged out by this and no existing test changes meaning.

That is not only about a new screen. Every time a dealer is given a right and phones to say it did
not work, this was the reason, and the answer was "log out and back in".

Rules R P2-4.2 (rewritten) and R P2-4.9 (new), two tests on top of the existing ones for the
rights check.

**Note for after the deploy:** your own session predates the change, so it carries no generation
and is left alone by design. Sign out and in once, and from then on it keeps up by itself.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
params.title: Werking hangs under Inzichten, and a granted right no longer waits for the next sign-in
